Thus I emended for ἀσφαλές [safe], which the scholiast interpreted as ἀσφαλῶς ἐπιδέτω με. ἐνώπια [may she look upon me safely. The walls]. But ἐνώπια [the walls] are said to be the walls of the temple, as ἐνώπια [the walls] are called by Homer the walls of the house that are opposite the door, as Od. 21, 121 τόξον μὲν πρὸς σταθμὸν ἐϋσταθέος μεγάροιο ἔκλιν᾿ ἑστάμεναι πρὸς ἐνώπια παμφανόωντα [he leaned the bow against the doorpost of the well-built hall, standing it against the shining walls], where Eustathius interprets τοὺς ἑκατέρωθεν τῆς εἰσόδου τοίχους [the walls on either side of the entrance]. A similar word is προνώπια [front walls].
